summary.title: MQTT broker from scratch #2 - Networking
summary.one_liner: You learn how to write MQTT packet packing functions in C (CONNACK, SUBACK, PUBLISH, ack packets) and build a single-threaded epoll-based TCP server with a callback-driven event loop.
takeaways: Packing functions mirror unpacking: they build a byte array from structs and unions, ready to be written to a socket.
A dispatch array indexed by packet type routes each packet to its pack handler; PINGREQ, PINGRESP and DISCONNECT use only a fixed header.
Static-buffer return values are fine single-threaded but will conflict in a multithreaded design, so malloc is suggested for later refactoring.
epoll is registered with EPOLLET and EPOLLONESHOT, and descriptors must be manually re-armed after each event, which keeps control over event handling.
Storing a closure pointer (callback, fd, args) in epoll_data.ptr lets each event call its own registered function; periodic tasks use timerfd.
summary.summary: The article continues a series on writing an MQTT v3.1.1 broker in C. It adds packet builder functions and packing handlers, using a function-pointer table indexed by packet type to serialize CONNACK, SUBACK, PUBLISH and ack-style packets into byte arrays. The second half sets up a single-threaded non-blocking TCP server on Linux epoll, with helper functions for socket creation, sending and receiving bytes. It finishes with an event loop abstraction that stores callbacks in epoll_data and supports periodic tasks via timerfd.
